messages:
sam: Upload from our private collector keeps timing out during the bundle upload. Collector v2.3.1, bundle ~420MB. Error in collector.log: "upload failed: timeout after 30s". Request id from collector: req_6f7a8b9c. No 403s, just timeouts. Can you advise repro steps we can run?

alice: Thanks — a couple quick checks: 1) can you paste the collector log lines around the timeout (5–10 lines before/after), 2) which upload method is used (S3 presign / SFTP / SCP), and 3) any proxy or corporate firewall in path? pinging @ben for infra. :eyes:

ben: Often this is either presign expiry, proxy idle timeouts, or multipart chunking issues. Sam, please try a curl repro directly against the presigned PUT URL the collector logged (mask any creds). Example curl we ask for: 

```
# replace PRESIGN_URL with the URL from the collector log (mask query params if needed)
curl -v --fail --show-error --location --request PUT \
  --header "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --upload-file ./sample-420mb.bin \
  --max-time 120 \
  "PRESIGN_URL"
```

Use --max-time 120 so we can see if longer timeout helps. Also get collector system logs: 
```
sudo systemctl status redwood-collector --no-pager
sudo journalctl -u redwood-collector -n 300 -o cat > collector.journal.log
sudo tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/collector.log > collector.tail.log
```
Include the manifest id (sha256) the collector created and the presign id if present.

marta: If curl fails with TCP reset or hangs, check any corporate proxy (explicit HTTP proxy env or transparent proxy) and MTU. For private deployments also check that the private control plane can still generate presigns (look for control-plane request id in collector.log). If you can reproduce with curl, save the full curl -v output (contains headers) and the exact timestamp so we can correlate.

sam: Sharing snippets — collector.log around the time: 

```
[2026-03-16T15:12:07Z] INFO upload: starting presign for bundle manifest=sha256:4f7d... id=presign_abc123
[2026-03-16T15:12:08Z] INFO upload: presign returned, starting PUT
[2026-03-16T15:12:08Z] WARN upload: PUT stalled after 30s, retrying (attempt=1)
[2026-03-16T15:12:39Z] WARN upload: PUT stalled after 30s, retrying (attempt=2)
[2026-03-16T15:13:10Z] ERROR upload: upload failed: timeout after 30s, aborting
[2026-03-16T15:13:10Z] INFO debugbundle: bundle generation failed upload_timeout
```
I ran the curl command Ben suggested (using a local sample file) — output: 

```
* Connected to s3.example-corp.com (10.1.2.3) port 443 (#0)
> PUT /signed/object?X-Amz-... HTTP/1.1
> Host: s3.example-corp.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-amz-request-id: req_zzxy123
* upload completely sent off: 420000000 out of 420000000 bytes
* About to connect() to 10.1.2.3 port 443 (#0)
* Connection #0 to host s3.example-corp.com left intact
* Recv failure: Connection was reset
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection was reset
```

No 403s. Looks like the server resets on us after the full upload. Any quick ideas?

alice: That reset points to a middlebox or upstream S3 gateway dropping long-lived connections after the upload completes. Two targeted repros: 1) try the same PUT with chunked transfer disabled/enabled, 2) try HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2. Example curl variants: 

```
# force HTTP/1.1, bigger max-time
curl -v --http1.1 --fail --show-error --upload-file ./sample-420mb.bin --max-time 300 "PRESIGN_URL"

# try explicit chunked transfer encoding (some proxies behave differently)
curl -v -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" --no-buffer --upload-file ./sample-420mb.bin --max-time 300 "PRESIGN_URL"
```

Also try splitting into a smaller test file (10MB) to see if small uploads succeed. If 10MB works but 420MB doesn't, likely a proxy/reset threshold.

ben: Please also capture tcpdump during the curl run so we can see resets: 

```
sudo tcpdump -w upload.pcap host s3.example-corp.com and port 443
# run the curl repro
sudo pkill -INT tcpdump
```
If you can't share pcap, at least share curl -v + server response headers.

collector-bot: Debug bundle generator started for manifest sha256:4f7d... (id=bundle_20260316_151207). Presign token expires in 60s.

marta: If this consistently reproduces, we can try two mitigations from our side: 1) extend upload timeout and use multipart presign (collector has a feature flag to use multipart PUT with per-part presigns), 2) allow control-plane to emit short-lived upload endpoints through a different gateway that supports long uploads. For immediate repro, please run collector with increased upload timeout: 

```
sudo systemctl stop redwood-collector
REDWOOD_COLLECTOR_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT=300 /usr/local/bin/redwood-collector --config /etc/redwood/collector.yaml \
  --debug > collector.run.log 2>&1
```
Then re-trigger bundle generation. If you can reproduce locally with curl, attach curl -v and collector.run.log.

sam: I can run the HTTP/1.1 and small-file tests this afternoon and capture tcpdump. I also see the control-plane logs show successful presign right before the PUT. I'll attempt the collector run with REDWOOD_COLLECTOR_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT=300 and report back. Thanks all. :pray:

alice: Perfect. Action items: Sam — attach curl -v outputs, tcpdump (or curl -v http header dump), collector.tail.log, collector.journal.log, and the manifest sha256. We'll escalate to eng if we can reproduce. If you want a short-term workaround, enable collector multipart presign in /etc/redwood/collector.yaml and we'll walk you through the config change.

ben: If you hit a corporate proxy that's O(30s) idle-killing connections, multipart should work around it. We'll standby for artifacts.

sam: Will upload artifacts to the private support bucket and post links here (masked).
